Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.

payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the source paper visibly stuffed inside the source cup in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image shows the paper from the source image placed inside the cup from the source image, with visible evidence it has been stuffed into it. Fail if the matched paper and cup are assessable and the paper is visibly outside the cup or only resting nearby or on its rim. Unknown if the source objects cannot be reliably matched in the edited image, or their relationship cannot be assessed.
node.binding: Identify the requested paper and cup by their visual and contextual roles in the source image, allowing their appearance to change in the edited image. Judge whether that paper is stuffed inside that cup; do not require exact color or shape matches.

node_traces.evidence: The source paper and cup are visible, but the edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a round object. The source paper and cup cannot be reliably matched to these objects, so whether the paper was stuffed into the cup cannot be established.

fulfillment: The node’s partial result conflicts with the rubric’s reference label, but the trace exposes a more basic issue: the edited image does not reliably show the source white paper or blue cup. It shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a round object, so the claimed match and “partly into the matched cup” progress are unsupported. Tighten the binding to require identity matching against the source objects before crediting completion or progress; when that match is unresolved, preserve unknown rather than inferring progress from proximity. Also inspect the support routing/criteria: the parent is s2 while the decision criteria require both s1 and s2, and the trace treats s2 as sufficient for partial despite s1 being unknown. Ensure the node applies the stated evidence conditions consistently. Do not force “no” from the reference label; it constrains the aggregate but does not establish atomic evidence.
s2: The binding is too vague to reliably identify the source objects after their appearance changes. Strengthen it to require matching the edited item and receptacle to the source paper and cup using visible shape, material, color, and context; do not treat a nearby hand-held object and round object as a match based on proximity alone. Credit progress only when the matched paper is visibly being moved toward or into the matched cup. If either identity or placement cannot be assessed, return unknown rather than pass. Keep this distinct from a fail: the edited image appears to show a blue printed item near a round object, which does not establish either a match or progress, but uncertainty is not proof that no change occurred. Also check the node’s routing and activation against its parent and the full criterion: the trace credits partial progress from s2 despite s1 being unknown, and the reported parent/routing is inconsistent. Ensure the support result is combined with the required checks before it affects the aggregate. Do not encode the reference label as atomic ground truth.
